text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps other developers work with it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions for variables and functions, so their purpose is obvious. Another important practice is keeping functions small and focused on one task. This makes the code simpler to test and debug. Clean code is also easier to maintain over time, because changes can be made without breaking other parts of the program. In short, writing readable and well-organized code saves time and reduces mistakes in the long run.
